info.album: She Loves You / A Hard Day's Night (A Tribute to the Beatles)

podcast.body: Co-written by John Lennon and Paul McCartney, this song, released in September 1963, marked The Beatles' significant breakthrough in Canada. It rapidly gained immense popularity, selling 100,000 copies and causing such a huge spike in demand that their earlier songs had to be reissued to meet the public's newfound interest. "Written by John Lennon and Paul McCartney, the song quickly exploded in popularity, selling 100,000 copies, and due to a huge spike in demand, the earlier songs were reissued, as the public now clenored for the Beatles."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This early hit by The Beatles features John Lennon's predominant acute voice accompanied by truly acute guitars, which was characteristic of the 1960s rock sound. While the band broke many rhythmic barriers, the preservation of acute sounds was not among the canons they overturned. "Vamos a escuchar si lo habéis llegado a una de las primeras canciones que hizo famosos a los Beatles, en las que vemos esa voz aguda que predominaba de John Lennon acompañada de guitarras verdaderamente agudas."

podcast.body: This song is referenced in a comparison by Lester Bangs, who questioned if "Sugar Sugar" by The Archies was truly that far removed from "She Loves Me" by The Beatles, suggesting a shared root with rock and roll. "Is sugar sugar by the Archies really all that far from she loves me by the Beatles?"

srcs.episode: Ep. 30 - The Sweet Sound of 70s Bubblegum Music

podcast.body: In March 1964, this song replaced "I Want to Hold Your Hand" at number one on the Hot 100, making The Beatles the first act to achieve this feat. Two weeks later, it was replaced by their own "Can't Buy Me Love," signifying the peak of their first American imperial highpoint. "In March of 1964, the Fab Four's She Loves You replaced their own hit I Want to Hold Your Hand in the number one spot."
